title: The eager PPTX slide catalog is parsed once per borrowed presentation, not once per catalog query
decision: retained, implemented in litchi-pptx; PPTX-4 measured and frozen as a design, not implemented
code_state: crates/litchi-pptx/src/presentation/{model.rs,package.rs} only; no public API, error type, limit or output byte changed; PresentationPart keeps Copy; no new unsafe and no new dependency
reason_codes: change 0587's PPTX-3 measured Presentation::slide(i) at 2.95 M Ir per call on a 200-slide deck because each call re-parses presentation.xml; this reproduces 2.83 M on the same shape and takes a 200-slide by-index walk from 566.0 M to 26.9 M Ir (-95.25%) and from 30.94 ms to 1.54 ms at p50 against a -0.39% A/A floor

the memo is value-identical by construction: the package and the main part are borrowed for the view's lifetime, so their bytes cannot change while the memo lives, and only successful parses and successful validations are memoized

the base's asymmetry is preserved, not repaired: slide() and slides() use the unvalidated catalog and slide_count()/slide_references()/write_text_to use the validated one, so no refusal moves; a test pins both fill orders
78 .pptx fixtures x every catalog-dependent public projection = 1,229 oracle rows per leg are byte-identical, including 11 AmbiguousSlideName refusals and 156 None results

PPTX-4's size gate is met by 4.6x to 9x (the raw budget scan is 15.4-37.1% of Presentation::text() instructions and 18.6-36.0% of its p50), but fusing the passes relocates two raw-byte limits, moves two refusals and weakens one defence, so it stops at a frozen design

accepted_evidence.counts: callgrind isolation pairs on a retained scratch probe, N=4 and N=24 on shapes.pptx and N=1 and N=4 on the 200-slide deck, differenced and divided, per leg, over thirteen operations
accepted_evidence.timing: paired ABBA (A1 B1 B2 A2), 40 samples per leg-run, taskset -c 13, over eight probe operations and the three selectors change 0587 named; a second 100-sample window re-ran the two eager filesystem selectors beside two controls this change cannot reach
accepted_evidence.value_identity: 78 .pptx fixtures under test-data, 1,229 rows per leg covering slide_references, slide_count, slide_size, slide(i) for i in 0..=count with partname, name and text sha256, slides(), find_slide by every observed name plus an impossible one, text() sha256, write_text_to length/sha256/report, content_parts, hyperlinks and slide_masters, each as a value or as the Debug form of the typed error; both legs sha256 11cecb07bdd63262536ad935db7b38dfb117231bbd498edb1b78277e3c088d70
accepted_evidence.tests: four new tests in crates/litchi-pptx/tests/pptx_slide_catalog_memo.rs, all four of which also pass on the unmodified base
accepted_evidence.reachability: callgrind of the filesystem child plus the facade source reading, showing that pptx_file_eager_slide_count and pptx_file_eager_selected_slide time the source-backed facade route, not the eager borrowed view this change edits
accepted_evidence.pptx4: a measurement-only checkout with scan_raw_semantic_text_xml removed, profiled and timed against the base on four decks, with callgrind_annotate inclusive attribution splitting semantic_text_from_part into scan, MCE and parse

accepted_costs.slide_references_clone: the public slide_references() returns an owned Vec, so it now clones the memoized catalog instead of moving the freshly parsed one: +46,971 Ir for 200 references (+785 for 6), about 235 Ir per reference
accepted_costs.single_query_timing: a borrowed view that makes exactly one catalog query is +0.78% to +1.98% at p50 against A/A floors of +0.59% to +2.80%, on paths whose instruction counts did not rise
accepted_costs.retention: the parsed catalog is held for the life of the borrowed view instead of for the life of each query; bounded by the existing MAX_SLIDES = 100,000 as one u32 and one relationship-ID String per slide
accepted_costs.instruction_counts: instructions rank work, not latency; callgrind counts rep movsb per byte and runs SHA-256 in software; one deterministic run per leg
accepted_costs.binary_layout: the two legs are separately linked binaries, and this corpus shows a +/-0.7% instruction spread between them that is not stable in sign

known_gaps.named_selectors_unreachable: pptx_file_eager_slide_count and pptx_file_eager_selected_slide, the two scenarios 0587 named for PPTX-3, route their timed query through PresentationImpl::PptxSource and never execute the changed code; both show a shift above the 5% review trigger that this change cannot have caused, reported and chased in a second window rather than averaged away
known_gaps.facade_reach: litchi::Presentation builds a fresh package.presentation() per method call, so a facade caller still pays one parse per query; lifting the memo to litchi_pptx::Package needs invalidation at every mutation door and is a separate design
known_gaps.find_slide_by_name: unchanged at +0.01% Ir; its cost is the per-slide c_sld_name MCE-plus-parse, which is PPTX-4 territory
known_gaps.real_producer_reach: no real 200-slide deck exists under test-data; the large deck is the harness's authored media-rich corpus, and the real fixtures carry 6, 11 and 19 slides
known_gaps.pptx4_not_implemented: the fused pass is frozen as a design with four admission conditions, including measuring what fraction of the corpus takes the MCE codec's presence fast path, which decides whether the saving transfers at all

withheld: any registered speedup, throughput, cold-cache, physical-I/O, range-source, allocation, RSS, concurrency-scaling, real-producer or cross-platform result
any claim that this change moves pptx_file_eager_slide_count, pptx_file_eager_selected_slide or pptx_semantic_full_text
any claim that the PPTX-4 prototype is shippable: it deletes an adversarial-input defence and is retained only as an upper bound
